Image 1: WARRIOR TO INSERT. This exact character is the primary identity/pose/pixel source. Keep the helmet silhouette, grey steel shade planes, small warm face, olive tunic, olive shield with steel rim, brown gloves/boots, diagonal short sword, spread bent-knee stance and facing unchanged. Preserve the actual pixel clusters as closely as possible. Use one identical-size copy in each of the four examples. Do not redesign/repaint the warrior, make it brighter, replace it with the tiny screenshot characters, add a red cape, new armor, or change its proportions. Match how this same warrior sits on the tile: visible warrior height about 72 units for a tile top 128x96, equal uniform scaling, same relative origin/foot location and orientation. Keep both feet/contact points in the same position within each tile, just below its visual center. Do NOT transfer the white background, rough cutout artifacts, holes or older grass rendering.

LAYOUT:
Four separate equal-size full diamond tiles arranged as a spacious 2x2 grid, each diamond top width:height exactly 4:3, same projection and scale, same height of cut-earth sides. Same intact full warrior sprite above each tile, same position/size/light, fully visible head, sword and shield, no cropping, plenty of separation between examples. Clean flat dark blue-grey background #293C48. No gameplay HUD, no large overall title, no border panels, no decorative frames.
Top left: grass. Top right: stone. Bottom left: shallow water. Bottom right: deep water.
Small simple labels below the four examples, EXACTLY: "Трава", "Камень", "Мелководье", "Глубокая вода". Text in #E7E6D6, no other text.

TILE ART:
Match the restrained newly selected PIXEL ART, large connected flat color planes, crisp square pixel steps of similar visual granularity to the warrior. Just a little coherent detail, not elaborate scenery: one small sparse grass clump and a broad dirt patch on grass; one or two short restrained chips on a single broad stone slab. No tiny bricks, texture noise, thin cracks everywhere, dithering, painterly smoothing, glossy 3D, bloom, excessive grass, extra props or creatures.
Grass palette #64785A/#7D9270/#98A286, dirt #978971/#A6967B; warm cut-earth sides #685844/#92775B.
Stone one broad grey-blue slab, #5D7078 shadows, #9DADB0 selective highlights.

Not a shoreline ribbon and not a rock pedestal. Sparse tiny angular surface reflection. The bottom must read slightly visible below water.
DEEP WATER IS ONE WHOLE TILE: full darker blue-teal diamond (#315361/#3E6570/#527F87), NO visible bottom, one or two short quiet reflection marks. Both water types have flat surfaces and clear whole diamond outlines, same footprint as dry tiles, no glass cube, waterfall or decorative shoreline. Water examples are a neutral sprite/color-readability comparison, not a depiction of game traversal rules. Dry tiles may have a very small soft-dark contact mark; no big directional cast shadow. scene_prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: ONE assembled tactical battlefield scene, 1600x1200 landscape, no HUD.
The user asks to build a full scene from these four tiles. Their latest explicit choice is COLORS AND NEATNESS OF IMAGE 1, CHARACTER-TO-TILE SIZE OF IMAGE 2.

INPUT ROLES — IMPORTANT:
IMAGE 1 is the PRIMARY STYLE/COLOR/MATERIAL REFERENCE. Preserve its calmer muted grass greens, less bright blue-green water, subdued grey stone, soft warm brown soil sides, and controlled pixel detail. Its small-character scale is NOT the selected scale.
IMAGE 2 is ONLY THE RELATIVE WARRIOR SIZE/PLACEMENT reference: use its visibly larger warrior relative to one terrain tile, approximately half the tile's width, with the same pose/gear/stance. Do NOT copy its brighter/more saturated colors. Do NOT further enlarge to some older placement example.
Both images show the same recognizable warrior with steel grey helmet/shoulders, olive tunic/shield, brown boots/gloves and short sword. Preserve this character appearance.

TASK:
Combine the grass, stone, shallow-water and deep-water materials into ONE cohesive connected 8x8 diamond-grid battlefield. This must be a single scene, NOT a 2x2 tile sheet, not four isolated platforms, not a collage. The board nearly fills the frame with comfortable dark background margin. No labels, no text, no HUD, no axes. Flat quiet #293C48 background.
Use a consistent steep isometric grid with top diamonds about4:3 width:height, same scale everywhere. Warm brown cut-earth sides only around exposed outer board edges/banks. Neighboring floor tiles connect into a surface; no gaps or separate pedestal sides between flat same-level cells.

SCENE COMPOSITION:
A simple open grassy field with a small flat stone courtyard/path around the middle-left, and a narrow watercourse running from the rear toward the front across the right-of-center region. A short connected stone causeway crosses it, using the same stone floor tiles rather than a new ornate bridge. No walls, buildings, trees, columns, furniture, traps, fire, acid or extra terrain materials in this scene: just these four supplied tile types.
Suggested 8x8 tile arrangement, each letter one whole cell (G=grass, S=stone, H=shallow water, D=deep water); rows run along the two consistent isometric grid axes:
GGGGHHGG
GGGGDDGG
GGSSHDGG
GGSSHHGG
GGSSSSGG
GGGSHDGG
GGGGDDGG
GGGGHHGG
You may subtly adapt the overall arrangement for a coherent clean composition, but keep the four materials, modest stone area and clearly connected/tiled water region.

WHOLE-CELL WATER:
Every shallow-water cell is a COMPLETE light blue-green diamond with faintly visible sand/stone bed throughout its interior, matching image1's "Мелководье". Every deep-water cell is a COMPLETE darker blue-teal diamond with no visible bed, matching image1's "Глубокая вода". Material transitions follow the shared straight diamond cell edges. Not an organic shoreline depth ribbon, not half a tile, not little decorative puddles. Thin quiet grid seams continue across water at the same scale as dry cells. Broad calm underwater color planes, one or two submerged stones total, sparse short angular surface reflection marks. No neon cyan, caustic web, glossy water, foam or soft realistic gradients.

CHARACTERS:
Place THREE copies of the reference warrior naturally spread apart, all fully visible and standing on dry floor: one on foreground-left grass, one on the central stone path, one on far-right grass. Same original stance/orientation, helmet/shield/sword design and pixel finish. Figure width about ONE HALF of its own tile width, as in IMAGE2; not the smaller scale in image1. Feet grounded near the tile center, compact contact shadow, no sprite overlap. Do not put characters on water or invent swimming/immersion rules. No new enemy designs, banners or selection bars.

ART:
Use the exact visual calmness of IMAGE1: restrained saturation, gentle terrain contrast, large connected pixel clusters, clean square pixel steps, no global sharpening. Keep very sparse clumps and broad dirt patches on grass; most cells should have quiet interiors, not repeated speckle patterns. Stone tiles are one broad slab each, occasional small chips, no tiny brick subdivisions. At most a few small grass tufts across the entire board, not a tuft on every cell. Same palette and material finish throughout, no new light source or color grade. The figures should be readable but not surrounded by a thick new outline or glowing rim.
The final should look like a tidy playable pixel-art scene assembled from image1's materials with image2's larger figure proportions. Concept preview only.
